facts.raw_span: two weeks of fever
generalized weakness, vague abdominal pain, vomiting, headache, body aches, and moderate nasal bleeding
a 2×1 cm submandibular lymph node
hepatomegaly (7 cm below the costal margin)
urea 18.8 mmol/L
creatinine 141 µmol/L
ferritin >40 000 µg/L
pancytopenia: hemoglobin 6.4 g/dL, WBC 1.7×10^3/µL, ANC 0.9×10^3/µL, platelets 2×10^3/µL
bilateral subdural hemorrhages without midline shift
bilateral pleural effusion, extensive pulmonary consolidation, thrombosis of the celiac artery with splenic infarction, mild hepatomegaly, and massive splenomegaly with infarction
13% abnormal blastoid cells of medium size with fine nuclear chromatin, unevenly distributed coarse basophilic granules, and occasional bilobed nuclei
bone marrow aspirate was hypercellular with 26% immature metachromatic blasts

concepts.why: The presence of abnormal blastoid cells, erythrophagocytosis, and trilineage dysplasia in the bone marrow aspirate, along with systemic symptoms and organ involvement, suggests a diagnosis of Histiocytic medullary reticulosis.

The presence of 26% immature metachromatic blasts in the bone marrow aspirate, along with pancytopenia and abnormal blastoid cells in the peripheral smear, suggests a diagnosis of Acute myeloid leukemia with maturation.
The presence of high ferritin levels, pancytopenia, and abnormal blastoid cells with coarse basophilic granules suggests a diagnosis of Acute promyelocytic leukemia.
The presence of splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, and pancytopenia, along with a submandibular lymph node, suggests a diagnosis of Hairy cell leukemia.
The presence of trilineage dysplasia, megaloblastic changes, and pancytopenia suggests a diagnosis of Myelodysplastic syndrome.
The presence of splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, and a submandibular lymph node, along with systemic symptoms, suggests a diagnosis of Systemic mastocytosis.
The presence of bilateral subdural hemorrhages, pleural effusion, and pulmonary consolidation, along with abnormal blastoid cells, suggests a diagnosis of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The presence of pancytopenia, abnormal blastoid cells, and trilineage dysplasia in the bone marrow aspirate suggests a diagnosis of Acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
The presence of splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, and pancytopenia, along with a submandibular lymph node, suggests a diagnosis of Chronic myelomonocytic leukemia.
The presence of splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, and pancytopenia, along with a submandibular lymph node, suggests a diagnosis of Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia.

rationales.F07: Elevated ferritin levels can be seen in certain hematologic conditions.
rationales.F08: Pancytopenia can be seen in various bone marrow disorders.
rationales.F11: The presence of abnormal blastoid cells is highly suggestive of acute leukemia.
rationales.F12: The bone marrow aspirate findings are consistent with acute leukemia.
